story: In Victorian London, a brilliant but unorthodox scientist reanimates a young woman, giving her a second chance at life. As she navigates society's strictures, she discovers the freedom—and danger—of forging her own identity. The film blends dark humor with gothic romance, inviting viewers to question what it means to be truly alive. Yorgos Lanthimos’s signature off‑kilter style promises a visually striking, thought‑provoking experience.
context_bullets: Adapted from Alasdair Gray’s 1992 novel "Poor Things".
A co‑production between Ireland, the United Kingdom, and the United States.
Made on a $35 million budget and grossed over $117 million worldwide.

before_watching.lead: Early development began in 2009 when Lanthimos met author Alasdair Gray in Scotland
before_watching.text: Development on the film began as early as 2009, when Lanthimos went to Scotland to discuss the acquisition of the rights to Poor Things with the author, Alasdair Gray.

before_watching.lead: Principal photography was shot in Hungary from August to December 2021
before_watching.text: Principal photography took place in Hungary from August to December 2021.

before_watching.lead: The film premiered at Venice and won the Golden Lion
before_watching.text: Poor Things premiered at the 80th Venice International Film Festival on September 1, 2023, where it won the Golden Lion.

author_voice.text: "He was a very lovely man. Unfortunately, he died just a couple of years before we actually made the film, but he was very special and energetic; he was 80-something [when we met], and as soon as I got there, he had seen Dogtooth and said, 'I had my friend put on the DVD, because I don't know how to operate these things, but I think you're very talented, young man.'"

"After the relative success of The Favourite, where I actually made a slightly more expensive film that was successful, people were more inclined to allow me to do whatever it is that I wanted, so I just went back to Gray's book and said, 'This is what I want to do.'"

"It was so interesting to be involved in how the film was being pieced together, from cast to department heads to what have you. Ultimately, Yorgos was the one making those decisions, but I was very involved in the process, which started during the pandemic; we were reaching out to people and casting and everything."

why_now: At a time when conversations about bodily autonomy and self‑determination dominate cultural discourse, Poor Things offers a fantastical lens on those issues. Its blend of period setting and modern sensibility makes it a timely exploration of how we define agency in a world that often seeks to control it.

metaphors.text: Rotten Tomatoes’ consensus calls the film a “bizarre, brilliant tour de force.”

intertextual_refs.text: Alasdair Gray told Lanthimos, after seeing the director’s earlier film Dogtooth, that he thought Lanthimos was “very talented, young man.”

production_trivia.text: The film was made on a $35 million budget and grossed over $117 million worldwide, becoming Lanthimos’ highest‑grossing film.

critical_consensus.summary: Critics lauded Poor Things as a wildly imaginative, genre‑bending tour de force, praising Lanthimos’ audacious direction, the razor‑sharp screenplay, and especially Emma Stone’s fearless, layered performance.

strengths: Yorgos Lanthimos’ direction, noted for its bold visual imagination and tonal daring.
Emma Stone’s performance, highlighted by critics as “hilarious, beyond‑next‑level” and “wonderful—vital, exploratory.”
verdict: A daring, genre‑defying spectacle that rewards viewers who embrace its eccentricity and thematic audacity.

questions: How does Bella’s reanimated existence interrogate notions of personal identity?
What does the film suggest about the relationship between scientific ambition and ethical responsibility?
In what ways does the retro‑futurist Victorian setting reshape our understanding of class and power?
debate_prompts: Does the film’s blend of grotesque body‑horror elements with romantic‑comedy tones create a cohesive masterpiece, or do the shifts undercut its emotional impact?
cta: Dive into Poor Things and witness Yorgos Lanthimos’ most daring, visually striking work yet.
title: Poor Things
